chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) regarding

A man who gave another man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf as a single Hajj, so it is permissible for him to perform Umrah with Hajj (Tamattu'). He said: Yes, he only differed in order to gain more merit and goodness.

key_terms.إِنَّمَا خَالَفَ إِلَى الْفَضْلِ وَالْخَ: He only differed in order to gain more merit and goodness
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: To perform Umrah followed by Hajj (Tamattu')

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for someone who pays for Hajj to have the agent perform Umrah as well?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling where the agent performing Hajj on behalf of another is permitted to perform Hajj al-Tamattu', with the additional Umrah serving as extra merit (*fadl*) for the payer. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the agent's voluntary addition of Umrah does not invalidate the core Hajj obligation but rather enhances the spiritual reward for the principal. The chain of narration emphasizes the permissibility of this flexibility in delegated worship, reflecting the practical ease granted in religious duties.
